items.prompt: How many students replied to the survey?

groups.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

parts.context: A professor discusses a student survey and a presentation plan with two students.

transcript.text: Come in, both of you. So, your survey on international students. How many people answered in the end?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: It took us three weeks to design the questions, because we kept changing our minds about what to ask.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: And my English teacher helped check the wording, so nobody would misunderstand anything.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: We sent it to two hundred and fifty students, but only a hundred and eighty replied.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Which is fine for a first survey. The main question was about what students find hardest when they arrive.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: Did you have trouble reaching students from different faculties?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: A little. Engineering students were harder to find, but the student union shared the link for us.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: And what came top?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: I expected language, but actually it was making friends. Nearly half said that.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Language was second, and accommodation came third, which surprised me because the university says it's well organised.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: That's useful. Universities often assume that accommodation is not a problem.
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: Exactly, and that's one reason why we want to include some direct quotations in the report.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: Did anyone say what helped them?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: Yes, a lot of people mentioned the buddy scheme, where a local student meets you at the airport. They said it made the first week much easier.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Good. Now, which of your findings will you highlight in the presentation?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We're going to focus on the part-time jobs. Many students want to work, but the visa rules limit them to twenty hours a week.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: That's a sensitive topic. Make sure you present the facts carefully and don't sound as if you're blaming anyone.
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We'll be careful. We'll just say what the students told us.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: Right. Structure. How will you begin?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: With a short story from one student, a boy from Peru, who spent his first week eating only bread because he didn't know where the supermarket was.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Memorable. And the data?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We'll show it in pie charts, not tables. Tables are boring and the audience is mixed.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: How long will you have?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: That's quite tight. You will need to practise your timing.
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We know. We've already timed the first half and it was far too long.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Twelve minutes, plus five for questions.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Make sure you rehearse. Where can you practise with a microphone?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: The language lab is free on Thursday afternoon, so we booked it.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: Good. What about handouts?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We'd like to give a one-page summary, but the printing budget is tiny.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Email it instead. Students never keep paper.
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: Then we'll upload it to the course website as well.
transcript.speaker: OMAR

transcript.text: I like that idea. Have you thought about what questions the audience might ask?
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We made a list, and we think the first question will be about the sample size.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: One last thing. Your conclusion must include a recommendation.
transcript.speaker: PROF REID

transcript.text: We'd recommend a longer orientation for the first month, with social events every week.
transcript.speaker: LENA

transcript.text: Excellent. See you at the presentation.
transcript.speaker: PROF REID
